headline: 207 caps, 125 goals: Lionel Messi retires from international football
summary: The Argentine legend ends a historic 20-year career with the national team, leaving behind a record-breaking legacy of World Cup and Copa América glory.
details: Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic career with the Argentina national team that spanned more than two decades.
The 39-year-old forward made a record 207 appearances for Argentina, scoring 125 goals and leading the team to a 2022 FIFA World Cup title and two Copa América trophies.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino paid tribute to the Argentine great, calling his career "extraordinary" and praising his magical talent and humility that will be remembered forever.
Messi's international journey began in 2005 and concluded with Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.
In a three-page handwritten farewell message, Messi expressed gratitude to his family, coaches, teammates, and the Argentine people for their support throughout his journey.
While his time with the national team is now over, Messi will continue his professional club career with Inter Miami in the United States.
caption:
An era ends. 207 appearances, 125 goals, and a World Cup trophy. Lionel Messi says goodbye to Argentina.

Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, ending a historic career with the Argentina national team that spanned more than two decades.

The 39-year-old forward made a record 207 appearances for Argentina, scoring 125 goals and leading the team to a 2022 FIFA World Cup title and two Copa América trophies.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino paid tribute to the Argentine great, calling his career "extraordinary" and praising his magical talent and humility that will be remembered forever.

Messi's international journey began in 2005 and concluded with Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.

In a three-page handwritten farewell message, Messi expressed gratitude to his family, coaches, teammates, and the Argentine people for their support throughout his journey.

While his time with the national team is now over, Messi will continue his professional club career with Inter Miami in the United States.

headline_marked: Dhaka to share load-shedding burden with [[rural areas to ease power crisis]]
headline: Dhaka to share load-shedding burden with rural areas to ease power crisis
summary: Prime Minister's Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman says the government is redistributing electricity to ensure a fairer distribution of power shortages across the country.
details: Prime Minister's Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman announced that Dhaka is now experiencing more load-shedding as the government aims to distribute the power shortage burden more evenly across the country.
Previously, the tendency was to prioritize electricity supply to Dhaka, leaving rural areas to bear the brunt of frequent and prolonged outages.
Following the prime minister's instructions, the government has adjusted load-shedding in areas served by the DPDC and Desco to redistribute saved electricity to rural regions.
This shift is intended to improve power supply to industries and other important consumers outside the capital, while reducing the outages in villages.
Zahed noted that while big cities require more electricity due to higher economic activity, the current approach ensures that rural areas are not unfairly penalized.
The current power shortage is attributed to fuel shortages, power-plant faults, maintenance issues, transmission and grid constraints, and rising electricity demand.
The adviser expressed hope that the amount of load-shedding will decrease significantly within a very short period as the government takes steps to ease the shortage.
caption:
Why is Dhaka experiencing more load-shedding? The government is redistributing power to ease the crisis in rural areas.

Prime Minister's Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman announced that Dhaka is now experiencing more load-shedding as the government aims to distribute the power shortage burden more evenly across the country.

Following the prime minister's instructions, the government has adjusted load-shedding in areas served by the DPDC and Desco to redistribute saved electricity to rural regions.

This shift is intended to improve power supply to industries and other important consumers outside the capital, while reducing the outages in villages.

Zahed noted that while big cities require more electricity due to higher economic activity, the current approach ensures that rural areas are not unfairly penalized.

The current power shortage is attributed to fuel shortages, power-plant faults, maintenance issues, transmission and grid constraints, and rising electricity demand.
